retired: the `log`-crate `Logger`'s methods; `nros::Logger` is `nros_log::Logger` since the rebinding, and its type alias was deleted by phase-482 W6
why: OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: There are TWO Rust `Logger` types in this repo and the facade exports the wrong one. `nros::Logger` is `nros_core::logger::Logger<'a>`, whose severity methods forward to the `log` CRATE (`log::info!(target: self.name, ...)`). The Phase-88 facade `nros_log::Logger` -- the one `<rclc/log.h>` wraps, the one `nros_node::NodeHandle::logger()` returns, and the one CLAUDE.md's issue-0589 rule names (`nros_log::nros_error!(nros_log::get_logger("<crate>"), ...)`, because `std::println!` recurses to death on Zephyr native_sim) -- is a DEPENDENCY of the `nros` crate that is never `pub use`d from it. So the type a user reaches through `nros::prelude::*` is the one that does NOT go through the `nros_platform_log_write` sink chain. On the signature itself: rclrs has no severity METHODS at all -- `Logger` is a handle and emission is the `log_info!` macro family. Ours are methods taking a PRE-RENDERED `&str`, not `format_args!`, because rclrs's macro formats into a `String` and there is no allocator here; the `nros_log` macros solve the same problem by rendering into a stack `FormatBuffer` sized by the `NROS_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE` knob (issue 1037; formerly a `buffer-size-<N>` Cargo feature). Phase 379 W3 should decide which of the two loggers the facade exports; W5 should decide whether the surviving one keeps methods or macros.
